L173: > As it stands, crafted base raid weapons are flat out better than Adept raid weapons. We're not happy with this current state and have changes coming in Lightfall that give the new Lightfall raid Adept weapons access to enhanced perks (note that this is not going to be full, freeform crafting). It’s a little complex, so please look out for more information to come when we’re a little closer to Lightfall's release.
L174: >
L175: >
L176: >
L177: > Future plans for Exotic Champion weapons?
L181: > We don't have specific plans to add anti-Champion mechanics to existing Exotic weapons. The goal of recent additions was to address some obvious holes in the options available, and we're happy with how that worked out. That said, we are building anti-Champion functionality into a new Exotic weapon in Season 19 and may revisit other weapons later if we see a need.
L182: >
L183: >
L184: >
L185: > King's Fall weapons have unorthodox perk pools. What are the team’s feelings about continuing to do this versus making custom raid perks to differentiate endgame rewards?
L186: >
L187: >
L188: >
L189: > We have guidelines for how spicy perk pools can be depending on the difficulty of the source of the weapon. For example, Trials of Osiris and raid weapons get to break our standard perk combination rules. The King’s Fall weapons push this to an extreme, and we're evaluating whether they're an actual balance issue (seems okay so far though).
L190: >
L191: >
L192: >
L193: > We intend raid origin traits to make raid weapons feel unique and may still make one or more perks that are exclusive to a new raid. Starting in Season 19, you will see a small number of non-raid weapons get access to perks from older raids.
L194: >
L195: >
L196: >
L197: > Does Outbreak Perfected truly have Persistence, or is it simply its recoil settling like any weapon?
L198: >
L199: >
L200: >
L201: > Outbreak does not have Persistence. It does have 90 recoil direction where similar weapons are in the 40-60 range, but more importantly it recoils like an Auto Rifle not a Pulse Rifle, which is part of why it feels so unique. This was a Destiny 1 bug that we elected to maintain in the Destiny 2 reprise of the weapon.
L202: >
L203: >
L204: >
L205: > The Cold Denial that Xûr sold with the accuracy Masterwork, does that actually improve its accuracy?
L206: >
L207: >
L208: >
L209: > Masterworks provide additional weapon stats to a stat already existing on the weapon. Weapons can't benefit from a stat they don't have, and only Bows have an accuracy stat. The short of it is no, an accuracy Masterwork won't have any effect on Cold Denial.
L210: >
L211: >
L212: >
L213: > Do stability perks such as Rapid Hit affect the perfect draw window on Bows?
L214: >
L215: >
L216: >
L217: > Yes, anything that affects the stability stat on a Bow will affect the perfect draw window.
L218: >
L219: >
L220: >
L221: > How was it for the Weapons Team to add subclass verbs like Head Stone, Chill Clip, and Incandescent to weapons? Did you enjoy syncing the two more closely in gameplay and builds?
L222: >
L223: >
L224: >
L225: > Subclass 3.0 verbs opened up a huge amount of design space for weapons. The perks we've already made are just the beginning.
L226: >
L227: >
L228: >
L229: > Why does only a subset of Exotic weapons tie into Subclass 3.0?
L230: >
L231: >
L232: >
L233: > We're not planning to tie every Exotic into Subclass 3.0 verbs, but over time we'll add functionality to several of them, starting with those that are strongly themed around damage types. We're currently looking at Seasons 20 and 21 for passes on this, but we don’t have anything more on this particular topic at this time.
L234: >
L235: >
L236: >
L237: > Are we going to be able to have multiple perks in each column on crafted weapons at some point in the future?
L238: >
L239: >
L240: >
L241: > We're investigating this for a possible future release, but it's a more complicated task than it appears at first glance. Nothing in the immediate future, but we will continue looking deeper into this.
L242: >
L243: >
L244: >
L245: > How do the extra perks on ritual rank resets actually work? Is there a cap to the benefit?
L246: >
L247: >
L248: >
L249: > We have a formula that determines the maximum number of alternative perks based on the number of resets. For example, here are the formulae for Valor:
L250: >
L251: >   * Left column: 1+(CLAMP((valor_reset_count+1)/2,0,(10*rand/2)%3))
L252: >   * Right column: 1+CLAMP((valor_reset_count)/2,0,(10*rand/3)%3)
L253: >
L254: > Ok, that’s pretty arcane.
L255: >
L256: > What this means is that the left column maximum perk count increases at first and third resets, and the right column increases at the second  and fourth resets. The maximum possible is three perks in each column, with the actual number randomized between one and the current maximum.
L257: >
L258: >
L259: >
L260: > There has been a lot of discussion on perk drop rates recently. I’d really like to know if all perks are truly weighted equally and randomized, or if certain perks (i.e., newer ones) have drop priority.
L261: >
L262: >
L263: >
L264: > Weapon perks are weighted equally under all circumstances. There are zero cases in the game where one perk is more likely to roll than another.
L265: >
L266: >
L267: >
L268: > I've heard that you're reworking 20 Exotic weapons in Season 19. Why so many?!
L269: >
L270: >
L271: >
L272: > We said we're touching 20 Exotics (both buffs and nerfs), but the extent of that varies quite a bit. From a substantial rework (e.g., Lord of Wolves) to a small but impactful change (e.g., Legend of Acrius), there’s a lot to cover, both big and small.
L273: >
L274: >
L275: >
L276: > Also, a small update on that number. 20 is out of date, and it's now 26. We always keep the list of under and overused Exotics in mind and decided to take on a big chunk of them in Season 19.
L277: >
L278: >
L279: >
L280: > What are the criteria for reprising Destiny 1 weapons in Destiny 2?
L281: >
L282: >
L283: >
L284: > It's important to note that it's impossible to simply copy and paste Destiny 1 content into Destiny 2. Because of engine changes and the significantly higher bar for art quality on current generation hardware, any Destiny 1 content has to be rebuilt from scratch. They're basically the same development cost as brand-new Destiny 2 weapons, and with some exceptions, we believe players significantly prefer new content over reprised.
L285: >
L286: >
L287: >
L288: > For raids, we'll always reprise an Exotic weapon associated with a raid when we bring that into Destiny 2. We'll select the six most popular Legendary weapons and reprise those, as well. One other thing, and this hasn't come up yet, but in the event that a raid didn't have an Exotic (or that Exotic has already come back), or there were fewer than five Legendaries, we get to make new weapons to match the raid.
L289: >
L290: > ### It’s a Numbers Game
L291: >
L292: > 【38†Image】
L293: >
L294: > Why does Adagio have to be different on so many weapons?
L295: >
L296: >
L297: >
L298: > It's actually not. Adagio is only branched two ways, specifically to prevent it from being too strong on Bows (one-hit kills for getting a single bow kill is way too strong) and Shotguns.
L299: >
L300: >   * Bow plus Shotgun: + 20% damage
L301: >   * Everything else: + 30% damage
L302: >   * Note that because of damage number rounding, it may be difficult for players to reverse engineer this in-game.
L303: >
L304: > What does Zen Moment actually do?
L305: >
L306: >

L100: Alright, I think we should get into the actual TWAB now, so let’s get to it, Guardians!
L101: ## Weapons & Things
L102: 
L103: First up, we are going to jump right into the Sandbox changes, so let me hand it over to one of our associate designers on the Sandbox team, Mercules!
L104: 
L105: > Hello everyone, Mercules here. We moved a good bit of the balance changes from Season 18 forward to the mid-Season patch of Season 17, so this will be a bit lighter of a weapons-Sandbox TWAB than usual. That being said, there are still some changes we're really excited about, so let's dive in!
L106: ### TL;DR:
L107:   * Buffed some under-utilized weapon archetypes:
L108:     * Scout Rifles and Heavy Grenade Launchers in PvE.
L109:     * High-Impact Auto Rifles.
L110:     * Lightweight Bows.
L111:   * Buffed multiple perks, fixed some bugged perks, and updated some perk descriptions to be more accurate.
L112:   * Buffed multiple Exotic weapons.
L113:     * Added intrinsic Anti-Champion functionality to some.
L114:   * Reworked a couple of Exotic weapons whose functionality was causing issues.
L115:   * Updated the perk pools for Dares of Eternity weapons and gave them a new origin trait.
L116: ### Global Changes
L117: 
L118:   * Fixed an issue introduced in the 30th Anniversary update that caused too much Heavy ammo to drop when running double Special weapons.
L119:   * Several weapon stats were previously hidden, which made fully evaluating weapons difficult.
L120:     * Airborne effectiveness, recoil direction, zoom, and aim assist are now visible in the weapon inspection screen.
L121: ### Weapon Archetypes
L122:   * Scout Rifles - We felt they could still use a bit of love in PvE.
L123:     * Increased damage of all Scout Rifles vs. Minor enemies (red bars) in PvE by 10%.
L124:       * This change is in addition to the baseline damage buff given in the Solstice balance patch.
L125:   * High-Impact (360 RPM) Auto Rifles - This sub-family of Auto Rifles has good damage output but low ease of use, leading them to under-perform compared to other options in the same engagement ranges.
L126:     * Increased base stability stat of all non-sunset High-Impact Auto Rifles by 6-12, depending on the weapon (numerically this may seem like a small change, but it noticeably changes the feel of the weapons).
L127:   * Lightweight Bows - This subfamily has languished compared to their higher damage counterparts for some time, in part due to difficulty hitting perfect draw shots, so we've made it a bit easier.
L128:     * Reduced base draw time by 5% (from 612ms to 580ms).
L129:     * Increased the “perfect draw” window (how long you can hold the drawn Bow before you begin to lose accuracy and damage, stability modifies this window).
L130:       * From .30s to .50s on the low end.
L131:       * From .55s to .80s on the high end.
L132:   * Hand Cannons - Fixed Dire Promise's zoom stat (got changed to 13 inadvertently, it's now 14 again).
L133:   * Glaives - Their interactions with some Exotic armor pieces can be confusing, so we've explicitly made some changes to align better with our stated goals.
L134:     * Glaive melee attacks can now activate the Exotic armor perks on ACD/0 Feedback Fence, Karnstein Armlets, and Necrotic Grip.
L135:   * Breech Grenade Launchers - Concussion grenades can no longer roll in the magazine slot (blinding grenades are a better option in the same slot that serves the same purpose).
L136:   * Heavy Grenade Launchers – These don't see a ton of support in PvE, so we hope this makes them feel a bit better as a DPS or yellow-bar clearing option.
L137:     * Increased damage vs. Majors and above by ~10% (excluding Parasite, which does not need to do more damage).
L138: ## Weapon Pools
L139: 
L140:   * Updated the perk pools for Dares of Eternity weapons and added an origin trait.
L141:   * Addressed an issue where playlist (Crucible, Gambit, and strike) weapons weren't randomizing individual perk column’s perk counts correctly based on number of resets.
L142: ### Perks
L143:   * The Gambit and Iron Banner origin traits were too specific to be generally useful, so they’ve both been redesigned.
L144:     * Invader Tracker (Gambit Origin Trait)
L145:       * Renamed Gun and Run.
L146:       * Redesigned functionality to give a sprint speed increase on multi-kills.
L147:     * Skulking Wolf (Iron Banner Origin Trait)
L148:       * Redesigned to activate on kills while at low health (so it will work in all PvP now).
L149:   * Ambitious Assassin has fallen behind perks with similar functionality (such as Overflow)—we’ve adjusted this to have a higher potential than before.
L150:     * Increased magazine overflow from 10% to 20% per kill on Primary weapons only (Special and Heavy weapons are still 10%).
L151:     * Increased overflow cap from 50% to 150%.
L152:   * Wellspring had an internal cooldown to prevent it from activating too frequently—we no longer feel this is needed.
L153:     * Cooldown has been removed, allowing for Rocket Launchers and Grenade Launchers to return more ability energy when defeating groups with a single shot.
L154:   * Perpetual Motion was triggering frequently enough to be annoying, so we disabled audio/visual feedback on perk activation.
L155:   * Lead from Gold wasn’t respecting the functionality of splitting the Special ammo picked up when two Special weapons were equipped.
L156:     * Now gives the correct amount of ammo to each weapon when two Special weapons are equipped.
L157:   * Concussion Grenades can no longer roll on breech Grenade Launchers.
L158:   * Veist Stinger was intended to grant ammo on weapons that support it, and charge/draw time on Bows only, this was inadvertently applying to Linear Fusion Rifles as well, making it too strong for an origin trait on them.
L159:     * Fixed a bug where it was applying a charge time reduction to Linear Fusion Rifles—it will correctly only refill the magazine from reserves when it triggers on these weapons.
L160:   * Zen Moment has always had a description that confused players (Particle Repeater too). Their descriptions have been updated to say what they actually do.
L161: ## Exotics
L162: ### Buffs
L163: 
L164:   * We’ve added anti-Champion functionality to several weapons, with the goal of giving more options for each Champion type, split across weapon slot and ammo type—we expect to do this from time to time in the future as well.
L165:     * Le Monarque
L166:       * Added intrinsic Overload to Poison Arrows.
L167:     * Thunderlord
L168:       * Added intrinsic Overload.
L169:     * Malfeasance
L170:       * Added intrinsic Unstoppable to explosions.
L171:       * Added +25 to the base airborne effectiveness stat (28 to 53) to match other precision Hand Cannon’s intrinsic bonus.
L172:     * Wish-ender
L173:       * Added intrinsic Anti-Barrier.
L174:       * Increased number of hits vs most targets from 2 to 3 (more hits against vehicles, still 2 against players).
L175:       * Increased damage vs. Champions, majors, and minibosses by 10%.
L176:       * Draw time decreased from 828ms to 820ms.
L177:     * Ticuu's Divination gets a free, small buff from the global lightweight Bow changes.
L178:       * Draw time decreased from 612 to 580.
L179:     * Legend of Acrius has fallen far behind other Heavy, short-range weapons and warrants a buff.
L180:       * Catalyst now grants the Trench Barrel perk in addition to its other effects.
L181:       * Different versions of the Exotic Paired Legendary Weapons didn’t have matching stats, so we have brought them up to parity.
L182:     * Calus Mini-Tool
L183:       * Increased airborne effectiveness from 23 to 28 to match MIDA Mini-Tool.
L184:     * MIDA Mini-Tool
L185:       * Increased zoom from 13 to 14 to match Calus Mini-Tool.
L186:     * Drang (Baroque)
L187:       * Increased airborne effectiveness from 21 to 23 to match standard Drang.
L188:     * Sweet Business
L189:       * Increased airborne effectiveness from 27 to 32.
